question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2 \}$ to $\mathcal{C} = \{ \mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2 \}$ is given below. Find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ given that $\mathbf{x} =2\mathbf{c}_1-6\mathbf{c}_2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275167/assets/aebf6ca2f909bc73f2491ccd7fcc9df9474e7f7a0234f14da7f35fce31adb73b.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}} = P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}} [\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{C}} .
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-4)(-4)-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \frac{3}{2} \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $\mathbf{x} = 2 \mathbf{c}_1-6\mathbf{c}_2,$ we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275167/assets/669a28bddde21ca9e3a281ed65f0158f9890c16f450f7700df67038c48eccef4.svg)

Now, we compute $[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \frac{3}{2} \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
